title: Simulating Student-Tutor Interactions with LLMs for Multilingual Math Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2506.04920v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the ability to generate formative feedback and instructional hints in English, making them increasingly relevant for AI-assisted education. However, their ability to provide effective instructional support across different languages, especially for mathematically grounded reasoning tasks, remains largely unexamined. In this work, we present the first large-scale simulation of multilingual student-tutor interactions using LLMs. A stronger model plays the role of the tutor, generating feedback in the form of hints, while a weaker model simulates the student. We explore 352 experimental settings across 11 typologically diverse languages, four state-of-the-art LLMs, and multiple prompting strategies to assess whether language-specific feedback leads to measurable learning gains. Our study examines how student input language, tutor feedback language, model choice, and language resource

translated_title: 基于大语言模型模拟学生-导师互动以实现多语言数学反馈
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）已经展示了在英语中生成形成性反馈和教学提示的能力，这使其在AI辅助教育中日益重要。然而，它们在不同语言中提供有效教学支持的能力，尤其是针对以数学为基础的推理任务，在很大程度上仍未被研究。在这项工作中，我们首次提出了使用大语言模型进行多语言学生-导师互动的大规模模拟。一个更强的模型扮演导师的角色，以提示的形式生成反馈，而一个较弱的模型模拟学生。我们探索了352种实验设置，涵盖11种类型学上多样的语言、四个最先进的大语言模型以及多种提示策略，以评估针对特定语言的反馈是否能带来可衡量的学习收益。我们的研究考察了学生输入语言、导师反馈语言、模型选择以及语言资源水平等因素的影响。
tldr: 该论文首次开展了大规模的多语言学生-导师互动模拟，通过强模型扮演导师生成提示、弱模型扮演学生，在11种语言、4个最先进LLM和352种实验设置下系统评估了语言特定的数学反馈能否带来可衡量的学习收益。
